macro_themes.stance_summary: All agree the midterms were a historic GOP rout. Sacks blames the war, Chamath a broken economy and anti-incumbent swing voters, Friedberg government spending, Jason chaotic execution.
Sacks says the Iran war drove the loss and Trump must end it; Chamath says the war mattered less than the broken economy.
Inflation rose from 2.4% to 3.7% on fuel costs and drove the affordability backlash; Sacks expects it to fall if the war ends.
Friedberg says the end of DOGE and ~$2T deficits keep the cost of living rising and lead to socialist policy outcomes.
Chamath says wage earners feel the economy is broken and want economic populism, suggesting federal taxes go to zero below roughly $125-150k; Jason pushes a $15 minimum wage.
Jason says the Liberation Day tariffs started Trump's approval slide; Sacks says they barely moved Senate odds; Chamath says tariffs may look good later if manufacturing revives.
Sacks ties Trump's approval to gas prices and expects Brent to fall toward $70 if the war ends.

Sacks expects a major Democratic push for a federal AI department and regulatory capture; Friedberg fears state control of AI; Jason puts extreme scenarios near 1%; Chamath says legislation would mostly constrain data center supply.

A roughly $4T sell-off on data center fears. Chamath expects a slowdown that favors hyperscalers; Sacks expects capex to hold in 2027 and the pipeline to shrink by 2028; Jason expects data centers to move offshore.
Friedberg reports that OpenAI disproved the exponential time hypothesis in hours, pending verification.
